items.title: Wilson "Willie T" Turbinton Interview, 1990-09
items.q: And then to have an opportunity to talk to him on a level that was totally different than you just inspirating him at a concert and trying to get some words in as a fan.

ctx.x: Do you have any special, one night that stands out in your mind as very special from the workshop? What is it, Rene?

The one night that I remember more than anything is the night that Ray Charles came to the workshop. I mean, we were playing, they had three levels to the workshop. And sometimes there was like a roof that we would go up and just stand up and when we would take our breaks. And when we came down, Ray Charles was in the audience. And for me, I was such a fan of Ray Charles, just to be able to play and for him to be there and stay as long as he did. It was just such a charge for me. And then to have an opportunity…
Will you talk just a little bit about the closing of the workshop and the demise of it, and what you recollect from maybe why it closed or those kinds of things?
